title: CSV Line Parser

statement.md: A vendor sends trade rows as CSV lines. Split each line into fields with these rules:

items: A field that starts with `"` is quoted: it ends at the next `"` that is not doubled. Inside a quoted field, `""` stands for one `"`, and commas are ordinary characters.
After the closing quote the next character must be a comma or the end of the line.
A quote in the middle of an unquoted field is an error.
An empty line has exactly one empty field.

statement.md: For each line print `N` on the first output line, where $N$ is the number of fields, then each field as `[text]` on its own line. If the line is malformed print only `ERR c` where $c$ is the 1-based column of the first offending character; for a quoted field that never closes, $c$ is the column of the opening quote.

inputFormat: First line: $q$. Then $q$ lines, each a CSV line (may be empty).
outputFormat: For each line either `N` followed by $N$ lines `[field]`, or one line `ERR c`.
hints: Write the scanner as a small state machine: start of field, in unquoted field, in quoted field, after closing quote.
Track the column of the opening quote so you can report an unclosed field.
editorial: [{"type": "p", "md": "The states are START (beginning of a field), UNQ (inside an unquoted field), Q (inside quotes), QEND (just after a quote inside a quoted field, which is either a doubled quote or the closing quote). Each character moves the machine; errors report the current column."}]
